summary: Mota Lava Airport is a small regional airstrip serving the remote Torres Islands, the northernmost island group of Vanuatu in Torba Province. It provides the only reliable air link between the isolated communities of Mota Lava, Ureparapara, Toga, and Merig, and the rest of the country. The airport plays a vital role in connecting residents to essential services, commerce, and healthcare available only on larger islands.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines fly to Mota Lava Airport?
A: Air Vanuatu operates scheduled turboprop services to Mota Lava, typically routing through Santo (Luganville) before continuing on to other Torres Islands airstrips.

Q: How long is the runway at Mota Lava Airport?
A: The airport has a single short gravel/paved runway suitable only for small twin-engine turboprop aircraft such as the Twin Otter and similar STOL-capable planes.

Q: Are there facilities at the airport terminal?
A: Facilities are extremely basic, consisting of a small shelter or terminal building with minimal amenities. There are no jet bridges or extensive services, reflecting the airport's role as a community airstrip.

Q: How often do flights operate?
A: Scheduled service is typically limited to one or two flights per week, and schedules can change frequently due to weather conditions and aircraft availability.
transport_tips: There is no public transport network on Mota Lava; the airstrip is within walking distance of Ablow village and most island accommodations. Arranging a local pickup in advance through your guesthouse or lodge is highly recommended, as vehicles are scarce and shared taxis are informal at best. Most visitors continue onward by small boat to neighboring islands like Ureparapara or Merig, which can usually be coordinated at the airport on arrival.
local_tip: Bring all essentials, including sufficient cash and any medications, from Port Vila or Santo before flying in—the Torres Islands have very limited shops and no banking facilities, so the airport itself is effectively your last supply point.
